title: Isolate settings patch smoke before service startup
summary: Enter an explicit productized AppData sandbox and detach global desktop logger handlers before constructing the settings-patch smoke service, verify all declared runtime and logger paths remain contained, then close temporary handlers and restore process state exactly.
reason: Remediate P2 AUDIT-FIND-W01-028. The smoke constructed DesktopAppService to discover its default pipeline before changing LOCALAPPDATA, which could prepare and lock a real user's product runtime and log despite the advertised temporary boundary.
behavior_before: DesktopAppService was constructed before LOCALAPPDATA isolation. Productized runtime roots and the global file logger could therefore be created under the caller's real AppData, then reused by the supposedly isolated service. The smoke also expected an obsolete command-result shape for a missing strict confirmation field.
behavior_after: Pipeline default discovery occurs inside a forced productized sandbox. LOCALAPPDATA, the product AppData override, productized mode, and global logger handlers are scoped and restored; every declared service runtime path and file handler is verified beneath work_root. Missing confirm_save is required to fail strict HTTP validation, while explicit false still exercises backend command denial evidence.
tests_added: tests/webview/test_webview_settings_patch_smoke.py: productized mode with a sentinel real LOCALAPPDATA leaves that sentinel absent, resolves the default pipeline inside isolation, and reports only work-root-contained runtime/logger paths.
tests/webview/test_webview_settings_patch_smoke.py: global desktop logger handlers are restored by identity after the smoke.
tests/webview/test_webview_settings_patch_smoke.py: missing confirm_save produces strict HTTP 400 field-required evidence while explicit false produces the backend-owned denied command result.
